## [0.11.0] - 2026-07-29

A **load-test correctness release**, with HTTP/2 as its new capability. The protocol work is the headline feature: the engine had set `CURL_HTTP_VERSION_2TLS` for a long time, but the linked libcurl never had HTTP/2 in it, so every request ran HTTP/1.1 regardless of what was asked for. The larger body of work is a pass over what a load test actually does and reports, and several of those findings were serious - a run could send four times the rate you asked for, the data-sampling slider meant the opposite of its label, and a pre-request script that signed a request sent it unsigned. The app side is a rebuild of the response viewer and the editors feeding it, plus a published documentation site.

### Added

- **Real HTTP/2 negotiation**, on both Send and load test. The engine's `curl` dependency now requests the `http2` feature, pulling in nghttp2, so the option the engine was already setting finally does something. A build-time test asserts the capability bit so a rebuild cannot silently drop back to a 1.1-only libcurl.
- **One Protocol control**, in the request builder's **Settings** tab, governing Send and load test alike. `Auto` lets ALPN negotiate; `HTTP/1.1` forces it; `HTTP/2` attempts h2 over TLS and falls back to 1.1 over plain `http://`, which is curl's own `2TLS` semantics and deliberately silent, since a URL is often an unresolved `{{variable}}` when you set the field. A **Default HTTP Version** setting seeds the protocol a new request starts with, as a write-time default only: changing it never alters a request already saved, because a global toggle silently changing every stored request's protocol would invalidate comparisons against historical runs.
- **The Raw tab shows the protocol that was actually negotiated**, instead of the hardcoded `HTTP/1.1` it printed before no matter what ran. Run history and a run's report show the protocol that was *requested*, since a load run makes many exchanges and has no single negotiated value.
- **Pre-request scripts can change the request before it is sent** - headers, URL, method and body via `pm.request`. Edits were previously discarded in silence while the scripting docs described the pattern as supported, so a request-signing script appeared to work and sent the request unsigned. A value the engine cannot send now rejects the whole edit rather than applying part of it, and says so in the response's Console tab.
- **Bulk import is one atomic operation.** Importing a Postman, Insomnia or OpenAPI collection used to fire up to hundreds of sequential creates from the app with a best-effort rollback, so a large import could fail partway and leave a mess behind. It is now a single `POST /import/apply`: the engine assigns every id and validates the whole payload before writing anything, so an import either lands whole or writes nothing.
- **Postman environment and globals exports import.** A `*.postman_environment.json` file was previously rejected as an unrecognised format, even though the on-by-default "Import environments & variables" checkbox implied otherwise. Globals merge into your existing set rather than replacing it.
- **`{{variable}}` completion in the body editors**, for JSON, text and GraphQL.
- **A Load Testing settings panel** raises the app's own connection, rate, duration and request ceilings, which were hardcoded as much as 10x below what the engine accepts, up to the engine's own guard limits. The engine gained matching settings for its error-store cap and live-chart retention, previously fixed constants.
- **MCP's `run_request` and `start_load_run`** accept the same `httpVersion` choice, so an agent can ask for HTTP/2 the way the app does.
- **A documentation site** at [athrvk.github.io/vayu](https://athrvk.github.io/vayu/), built from `docs/` with MkDocs Material.

### Changed

- **Run time series are stored as one row per tick plus a run summary**, rather than a row per metric per tick. A page boundary could previously split a single tick across two pages. Runs recorded before this change still render exactly as before, and the API response shape is unchanged.
- **The response viewer was rebuilt** - tabs, toolbar, Raw, Console and Tests - and the timing views consolidated behind one shared module, replacing five copies of the phase logic. The toolbar shrank from 44px to 32px to match the tab strip, table rows from about 36px to 28px, and the view-mode control became keyboard-navigable instead of three plain buttons that ignored the Roundedness setting.
- **Denser request chrome, and descriptions render as markdown.** Section tabs went from 37-53px to a consistent 24px, the method moved into the URL field as a dropdown, and the description became an **Info** tab rather than a second header row on every request. Descriptions from imported collections now render as markdown, with links opening through a validated system dialog rather than as a live anchor in the renderer.
- **The key/value editor behind Params and Headers was rebuilt**, cutting each row from 48px to 36px.
- **Create and update are separate verbs** across collections, requests and environments, under one null-vs-absent rule: on create, absent and `null` both mean "use the default"; on update, absent means "keep" and `null` means "reset". A field with no default rejects `null` with a 400 rather than ignoring the write.
- **Settings entries can be a labelled picker**, not just a number or a toggle. A new `enum` config type with an `options` column of `{value, label}` pairs backs the Default HTTP Version setting and is available to any future picker-style setting.
- **A run's redirect policy is reported by the API.** `followRedirects` and `maxRedirects` have been stored on every run since 0.10.0 but never left the database; they now ride with `httpVersion` into `GET /runs`'s summary and a run's report. No screen displays them yet - this makes them available to anything reading the API.
- **One auth editor and one mode registry** serve both the request and collection hosts, and the pre-request and test script panels are now one shared component.
- **Toasts** are built on the shadcn/Radix primitive, theme-aware, and no longer sit on top of the Dock.

### Fixed

- **A load test could send up to four times the rate you asked for.** The per-worker rate limiter enforced its cap independently on each worker thread instead of splitting the aggregate target across them, so a 100 RPS budget could land near 400 RPS on the wire.
- **The data-sampling slider meant the opposite of its label.** The UI reads it as "keep this percent of successful responses"; the engine reads the same number as a sampling period, keeping 1 in every N, and nothing converted between the two. Setting the slider to 100% told the engine to keep 1% of traces. Only the shipped default of 10 was correct, by coincidence.
- **Out-of-range load-test settings could take the engine down.** Values from `POST /runs` went into casts and modulo operations with no bounds check, so dragging the sampling slider to its "0% - errors only" stop sent a zero and killed the daemon along with every other running test and live stream. Those fields are validated before a run is created, with a 400 and a reason; the slider's floor is now 1%.
- **A constant-rate run undercounted its own rate, could overshoot its deadline, and misread duration units.** Per-tick demand was truncated to whole numbers, so 1500 RPS delivered 1000; the final tick could push a backlog past the run's end; a descending ramp underflowed and flooded the target; and a duration written `"5m"` was read as 5 seconds. Rates now carry fractional demand between ticks, a run stops at its deadline with the shortfall recorded as dropped, and unit suffixes are honoured. The renderer only ever sent whole-second durations, so the unit bug was reachable mainly through the MCP tool.
- **Failed-request counts were always zero.** Integer division truncated any error rate below about 5%, so most real failure rates rounded away. A shared latency histogram was also written by every worker without the atomic API, losing samples under concurrent writes, and the per-run error store had no cap.
- **Stopping or deleting a run did not stop it.** A stop still drained the whole queued backlog and waited on every in-flight request, which against a hung server could be indefinite. Delete had no check at all and removed the row from under a worker still writing to it. Stop now cancels in flight and records each cancelled request rather than dropping it from the totals; delete stops the run first and returns a 409 if it cannot settle.
- **Stopping the engine mid-run could crash it or corrupt state**, because the run's worker was detached rather than tracked and shutdown could tear down the database underneath it. Workers are owned and joined in an ordered shutdown, and starting a run while shutting down now returns a 503 instead of accepting work nothing will execute.
- **A run configured near the ceilings could try to pre-allocate around 450GB** for its metrics buffers and throw during setup. Because that happens after the run's row is written, the run then sat showing "pending" forever instead of surfacing an error. Pre-allocation is capped; ordinary runs are unaffected.
- **Malformed writes were accepted and then silently discarded.** A create or update could store any shape for an object field, and every reader downstream ignored it - worst of all `auth`, which resolved to "no auth", so a request the user believed carried credentials went out bare. These now return a 400 naming the field instead of a false 200.
- **Load-test responses had no size cap**, a GET with a body was silently sent as a POST, a HEAD with a body likewise, and timing on a failed transfer could go negative. Buffering is now capped, GET-with-body is sent as GET, HEAD-with-body is refused with a clear error rather than rewritten, and failed-transfer timing is clamped.
- **Bulk-editing Params could wipe them.** Pasting a header-shaped line matched nothing in the `key=value`-only parser and wrote an empty list over your params with no warning. A valueless param like `?page` was dropped on load and reintroduced as `page=` on save, disagreeing with the URL actually sent.
- **Switching a body between JSON and GraphQL could destroy it.** Both modes stored to the same field, so a GraphQL parse failure on a JSON payload rewrote it as an escaped string with no way back. GraphQL now keeps its own draft per open tab.
- **Choosing GraphQL added a `Content-Type` header that was never removed** when you switched away, including to no body at all. It is now removed automatically, while a `Content-Type` you typed yourself is left alone. A header saved before this fix still needs removing by hand.
- **A newly added variable could jump above older ones.** `createdAt` was dropped when variables round-tripped through a send, and the app then re-stamped the undated row at save time, after the new row's own timestamp.
- **Response tabs disappeared when a response had no data for them**, which could leave a selected tab pointing at nothing and the pane blank. All tabs now render and show an empty state. The Raw tab, previously a dead path with no highlighting, shows the exchange in curl-style notation, and Console output loads as you scroll rather than being capped by rendering cost.
- **As little as a third of a drawer row responded to clicks.** The row painted hover and selection across its full width while the handler sat on a narrower button inside it.
- **Timing views had three display defects**: the waterfall drew two of its five phases in colours that collided with other UI under some accent schemes, rounded any sub-millisecond average to a flat "0", and History could show a "Timing Breakdown" heading with nothing under it.
- **Borders and separators invisible in dark mode** across the response pane - the timing tab's dashed separator and info dots, the outline around image, PDF and binary previews, and the console and error-detail slabs.
- **Tooltips open after a consistent 150ms.** The dock and collection tree had unintentionally reset the delay to Radix's 700ms default.
- **A failed collection save could be blamed on the wrong collection**, because the Info tab did not clear its error state when you switched away.
- **MCP's `start_load_run` advertised an `httpVersion` argument and ignored it** when the run named a saved request. The value was read on the ad-hoc, URL-only path; the `requestId` path composes its payload from the stored request, which always carries a protocol, so the run went out at whatever the request had saved and nothing reported that the argument had been dropped. It is now read alongside the other stated overrides, which both paths share.

### Internal

CI now builds and tests only the parts of the tree a pull request touches, cutting an app-only run from roughly 12-16 minutes to about 4. A daemon crash no longer leaves a run stuck as "running": startup reconciles it to "failed". The documentation site gained a design pass, a product-oriented home page and SEO metadata, and two READMEs plus the site FAQ were corrected for claiming Postman environment import before it existed. `docs/architecture.md` claimed the engine's libcurl gave "HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3" - wrong before this release, since HTTP/2 was not linked, and still wrong after it, since HTTP/3 is an explicit non-goal requiring ngtcp2 and nghttp3 and pinning the TLS backend to OpenSSL. The auto-save documentation was corrected for describing a deleted constant and a return field that never existed. CLAUDE.md gained two rules earned this cycle: never add an AI as a commit co-author, and scale verification to what a change could actually break.
